column8: Fri 20 Nov: 2.0 or 2.3, one clause of pedigree (Black 1980: whoever owns the leftover carries the fund's gains and losses); fix the use: for Laura a gain behind the ten reaches only her, but a loss beyond what is left would fall on the residency, since no money comes after January 2028 (idea 1b; case l.63-65); say IPS l.11's words, only money not yet promised goes into shares, never her own money; never imply Caplet drew on Black.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3, the break in one clause (a pension's owners and pensioners are kept apart by law; Laura is both, so her rule must carry its reasons); fix: IPS l.17's two reasons are exits for when the plan cannot be carried out, not the fence; the fence is l.11's rule, held by l.17's a fall in the market is not one of them; say the rule keeps them apart, never a legal ring-fence; add no rule (CANON A34).

Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q191-001: adds only that a fixed promise cannot share gains, which row 1 carries; Black's own asymmetry runs the other way (pensioners pressing for more), so the parallel breaks on its own disanalogy.

Fri 20 Nov: store only, the record that Black's headline case was tax; backs row 5's turn and the rule that the report never gives a tax reason (taxes are out of scope in the case); never the 49% or $2 million figures in the report.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3, one clause with row 13: the founder of the bonds-only case said that without tax the owner would not care, and Laura must care because nothing outside the portfolio may reach the payments (case l.91-92); answers why not shares with six years to wait without a tax word; one outside name per part, never in 3f.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c or 3d's reserves, one clause of pedigree for the conceit (promise capacity is what is owned); fix per this morning's judges: the bottom and the top rest on the late-2032 fund (IBTM), fund shares held for her that pay their net asset value with no predetermined amount, so say held for her in the late-2032 Treasury fund and counted with the range rule's 0.5% margin, never what she owns in Treasuries; never in Laura's words.

Fri 20 Nov: store, at most 3a's evidence; fix: in 2027 most of each payment is bought, and the top-up ($2,388) and the extra Treasuries come in January 2028 (NUMBERS headline), never the ten are bought in 2027; Laura's plan holds no shares at all in 2027, so keeping shares away that year is no choice; Keel inference, marked.

Fri 20 Nov: store, at most a pedigree clause beside the order-of-purchase reserve (2.3 or 3e): new money behind promises buys bonds first; Black put all new money into bonds for tax, while the 2028 deposit's later part buys the late-2032 fund and VT, so never the same rule.

Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q1c-023: its use is IPS l.9's career-as-holding root, which Bodie, Merton and Samuelson already carry, read on the page; Tepper integrates a company with its fund, a person's earnings only by analogy.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 with rows 5 and 13, the condition that transfers (owners are indifferent only if they can offset on their own account); fix: Laura has income and resources outside the portfolio (case l.61-63), so the reason she cannot offset is the case's rule that no outside money may meet the payments (l.91-92) and none is added after January 2028 (l.63-65), plus no margin in the plan; never she cannot borrow as a fact of her life.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q191-001 (the fund as part of the owner's own wealth, Black's as if); fix if used: held for her, never in her own name's portfolio.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q191-004: Tepper's half of the same tax case; store only.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3, the turn in one clause: Tepper said shares in a pension fund need imperfect markets to justify them, and Laura's imperfections (a career she cannot sell, no outside money for the payments, none added after January 2028) keep shares away from her promises; an inference from his sentence, marked; say the case's rule rather than no borrowing.
Fri 20 Nov: store only, background: Sharpe (1976) is read only as Tepper reports it; never in References until read.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q191-016: EMS's first-order result; the report gives EMS one clause at most, the zero sum.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 or 3a, one clause; figures check (NUMBERS 8s: 6,453 of 200,000, 1 in 31.0, median $27,695); fix: the 1 in 31 is spine row 10's aha in 3f, told once, so in 2.3 or 3a give the zero sum without the figure or point to 3f; any figure names the 27 September model (US shares at 6.7% a year), MODEL, never a plan figure; the reason the first plan was dropped stays IPS l.9's (CANON A3).
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q191-016, which already quotes EMS on default risk.
Fri 20 Nov: store only: costs barely apply to Laura (T-bonds no fee, iBond funds 0.07%, VT 0.06%, NUMBERS 0), so her case stands on risk; fees check.
Fri 20 Nov: store only: a company's taxes and agents, neither of which Laura has.

Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q191-001 (the owner holds the net value after the promises); a partisan source; never call the ten Laura's debts, since she owes the portfolio nothing in law (Q97-041's note): say her commitment.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 or 3a, one clause, the card's rarest: Boots cut risk in its pension so the company could carry more, and the IPS's last line draws that line through one life (no risk with the promises, risk on the page); the break, she never chose her career's risk, is IPS l.9's own reason; never in 3f or Laura's words; never a natural hedge.

Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q150-002 (the covenant test, pedigree not aha, cold test 8): adds Ralfe, Speed and Palin's name for it, double jeopardy; say can fall, never fall together (card Q50); co-sponsors fund the building, never the ten (case l.91-92).

Fri 20 Nov: store, at most a clause beside aha row 3 (Boots's architects called their timing luck, as the team tells its fills); fix: never needs no timing at all or at whatever they cost: the plan needs the year, not the day, holding unless yields fall about 3.6 points before January 2027 (aha row 3; NUMBERS 5); Q68-011 holds the trustee chair's version.
Fri 20 Nov: store: a thin parallel (Boots locked a surplus, Laura a price); figures check (roughly $300,000, IPS l.13; $302,287 and the $2,388 top-up, NUMBERS headline).

Fri 20 Nov: 3a with row 26, the event (the first all-bond pension moved 15% out of bonds in May 2004); read in part (paywalled), so quote only the openings; never set it against IPS l.17 as only two things can break the plan.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a, one clause: the step back's reason was the bond market's reach, which cannot touch ten payments ending in 2042 (sharpens Q68-028); fix per this morning's judges: five of the ten rest on iBond funds that pay their net asset value, so say each has a Treasury bond or a Treasury fund that ends before it, never each has a Treasury maturing before it; the IPE page is undated.
Fri 20 Nov: store only: partisan voices on both sides; serves no part.
Fri 20 Nov: store: a coincidence of dates, no cause; at most beside Q93-027's 2.2 clause, which keeps its fixes (no Treasury bond, four payments forced, 2037 a choice).

Fri 20 Nov: merged into H7-009 (a home-made buy-in with no insurer; she starts where pensions end scored 2.7 cold): adds Boots's 2023 buy-in as a pension's end state; never in that state or insured for Laura's reserve, since five payments rest on fund payouts at net asset value with no predetermined amount; say no payment relies on money still to come from January 2028.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a, one clause on why the match is complete when bought: Boots committed about £500m more in 2023, while Laura adds nothing after January 2028 (case l.63-65), hence the extra Treasuries sized so the ten are paid even if cash waiting earns nothing (NUMBERS 2); never blame 2004, never a recovery plan.
Fri 20 Nov: store only: unlike measures (Boots's whole fund against VT's 6.58% of the $450,000 at cost, NUMBERS 8g), so never in the report.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.0, one clause of pedigree beside the spine; fix: say the pension-fund case for bonds (Black 1980, on tax; Exley, Mehta and Smith 1997, without), never the rule pension economists reached, since Black's rule was all bonds; the reasons are IPS l.9's and l.11's, and l.17 is an exit list, not the fence (row 2); Keel synthesis, never claim Caplet read these papers.
Fri 20 Nov: store only: qualifies row 26 (a 50-year gilt a year later); never tie it to Boots or pension demand.
